rows.call: The farm's gates
rows.decision: A crop opens at its Farming level and nothing else. Soil tiers are removed. Watering lives inside Tend the field and there is no water button on a bed. Every seed row and Tend result says what the harvest is worth to the hunt. Potato gets a hunt consumer in Wheat's ration recipes or is removed with the dead rows.
rows.reason: Four gates on one crop is three too many. One press that harvests, replants and waters is the farm with the chore taken out.
rows.evidence: COMPUTED: the soil tiers are a 130,500 gold sink in all, which is small beside the House re-read of CE-5. A full field makes about a four's daily drink bill (chapter 07 section 2.6).
depends: GR-34 (Potato, if it finds no consumer)

rows.call: Home looks and visiting
rows.decision: Three home looks: a cottage for the Camp, Homestead and Farmstead, a manor for the Manor and the Keep, a castle for the Castle. Two new maps, drawn so a clan hall can reuse the tiles. Visiting is look-only, one read and no polling, open to friends and clan members, and it opens from the Homestead once the Hall of Firsts exists.
rows.reason: Ground art is what limits how fast the world grows, and three maps spent on the home are three regions' grounds delayed. A wall nobody can visit until the Castle is a wall nobody sees for the first two months.
rows.evidence: EVIDENCE: study 58. COMPUTED from chapter 02: a region is needed every 45 to 53 days and no lane says who draws them. Nothing here can be measured on the matrix.
rows.replaces: 26-3 (a map for each deed) and 26-11 (visiting opens at the Castle), both 2026-11-20
depends: MM-18 ("party member" has no meaning once a party is your own four, mmo decider)
The art director (the Camp's name against its picture)

rows.call: House room rungs
rows.decision: House rooms sell kept materials, never speed, and the swap is built ahead of the lining work. If it cannot be built at once, the speed rungs come off sale until it is. Each rung's row says who it is for.
rows.reason: A rung that costs gold and never pays back is a trap, and the first player to do the sum tells everyone. Kept materials is worth more the costlier the recipe, so it stays worth buying at every tier.
rows.evidence: MEASURED: the swap is an identity for the hunt, and the sixteen speed rungs cost 5.25M and never pay back (study 58). COMPUTED, not played: rungs 2 to 5 pay back in about 120 bench hours on a room's best recipes.

rows.call: Seeds from monsters
rows.decision: A sample of one, not two. The Moonbloom seed leaves the Shop and becomes a tradable Rare row on one Morrow Hills ground, inside that ground's six Rare rows. Its drink sits on the existing ladder at the next step and never above it. A second seed is written only after the first has been read in play.
rows.reason: A Rare line that is not gear and that a farmer wants to buy is a good idea worth one honest test. Moonbloom already exists as a crop, so the sample costs one drop row. Nobody has named the second seed, and inventing one to make the sample two is content for its own sake.
rows.evidence: EVIDENCE (patch home-2 on the uncalibrated harness, direction only): a four on all home-made supplies levels about 6% faster, about 10% on Deadly. That is why the drink never sits above the ladder. HYPOTHESIS that players plant or trade the seed. What overturns it: if the seed's book has no fills and under one account in ten plants it, no second seed is made.
depends: The region lane (which ground carries it)

rows.call: Tamsin's task for a ground is taken when a hero enters it.
rows.decision: Yes. Taken on entry with no press. The pay is collected on the end card or by Carry on.
rows.reason: Nobody decides whether to take a free task, so making me press for it is a press with no decision in it.
rows.evidence: EVIDENCE: 3,251 wolves were killed that she would have paid for (60 GR-78). Task rows checked in src/data/tally-tasks.js.

rows.call: One table, the Path, says when every system opens, and the first hour teaches four heroes.
rows.decision: Yes, the Path and chapter 08's first hour: one hero alone to Level 5 in the Mill Cellar (about minute 17), then three more heroes made in one flow. The three recruits each run their own Mill Cellar hunt, alone, and one Start begins all three (GR-80), while the first hero hunts Meadowbrook Thicket. Then all four enter the Millrace Sewer at about minute 36 on one Start. The pre-filled company always holds one healer, and the creation screen says so before a player changes it. Additions. (1) The doors chapter 08 left open: chat and the presence strip from the start. Clans can be joined from the first day. The calendar banner shows after the first stamina end. The world boss opens at Level 13 for each hero sent. The Even Arena at Level 20. The Open Arena at Level 30. The clan board when you are in a clan. Factions at the first Krell kill as ruled. (2) If the core decider's check C3 fails, the four's first hunt together is Meadowbrook Thicket and the Sewer card moves to the Level where C3 passes. That is a data row, never tutorial math. (3) Chapter 06's minute 5 picture is corrected to one hero, with Global chat open and the strip on the Cellar card.
rows.reason: Four name screens before a single kill would lose people, and four bars at once teaches nothing. One hero for 17 minutes teaches the loop, and then "you have three more" is the best surprise of the first hour. The MMO doors are spread out so every few Levels names a new thing and Level 10 is not a pile.
rows.evidence: PLAYED twice for minutes 0 to 17 as a one-hero opening (chapter 08 section 2.1). From minute 17 it is designed and unplayed. My walk-through re-check against src/data on this branch is in the md mirror. HYPOTHESIS for the doors (TARGET Levels). Overturned by check C3, by the blind first hour (playtest 12) and by playtest 1.
rows.depends: CORE DECIDER: step 13 stands on check C3 (a start-kit four holds the Sewer on Normal at Level 5, Rat King room included, no death in 4 seeds of 8 hours). Also C1 and C2. Items decider fills Path rows for Levels 17 to 29. Economy decider: the account's 500 gold granted once (GR-8). MM-4 and MM-14 numbers must exist before the boss and arena doors are final.
rows.was: Yes, the Path and chapter 08's first hour: one hero alone to Level 5 in the Mill Cellar (about minute 17), then three more heroes made in one flow, who run the Cellar together while the first hunts Meadowbrook Thicket, then all four enter the Millrace Sewer at about minute 36 on one Start. My additions. (1) The doors chapter 08 left open: chat and the presence strip from the start. Clans can be joined from the first day. The calendar banner shows after the first stamina end. The world boss opens at Level 13 for each hero sent. The Even Arena at Level 20. The Open Arena at Level 30. The clan board when you are in a clan. Factions at the first Krell kill as ruled. (2) If the core decider's check C3 fails, the four's first hunt together is Meadowbrook Thicket and the Sewer card moves to the Level where C3 passes. That is a data row, never tutorial math. (3) Chapter 06's minute 5 picture is corrected to one hero, with Global chat open and the strip on the Cellar card.
rows.fixNote: Check C2 was run by the review and fails. Three new heroes together in the Mill Cellar earn 0.53 times what one earns alone, because the Cellar is spawn-limited. Alone, each recruit levels at the first hero's pace, so minute 36 stands.
rows.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS. This is the review's own design and nobody has played it.

rows.call: One Start, one plan and one return card for an account's four heroes, and a job queue.
rows.decision: Yes, all of it. One plan for each hero shown as one card for the account, any line set once and applied to all four. Carry on is one press for the account. Own heroes form a party with no invite. One return card with at most three things that need a decision. A rest plan of up to three job steps that never loops and ends in "wait in town" or "hunt again, once". A starting loot plan and a starting rest plan so a new player edits and never builds. None of this is ever Premium.
rows.reason: Starting and stopping four heroes one at a time is the same decision four times, twice a day, forever. This is the feature that makes four heroes a party and not four chores.
rows.evidence: RULED 27-1 (Carry on) and the first principle. TARGET: a visit under 4 minutes and zero repeated-decision presses (standards X9, X10). Chapter 09 counts about 20 presses a day in place of 100, COMPUTED.
rows.depends: Systems engineer: one Start is one intent the server expands through the same checks. GR-1 (town work in closed form). GR-48, GR-57, GR-58 in other areas.

rows.call: A hero may move to the next ground when it outgrows this one, if you chose that.
rows.decision: No. Keep 27-1 whole: no hunt ever starts by itself. When a ground is outgrown the hero goes to its rest plan and works in town. The return card puts "outgrown, go to the next ground" first under Needs you, as one press for the whole party.
rows.reason: It is a small win that breaks a clean rule. Only one ground in the game ends itself at a Level today, and the first hour already walks me through that moment by hand. With the job queue an outgrown hero is working in town, not standing around. And a party starting a new ground by itself while I am away is when deaths are most likely.
rows.evidence: EVIDENCE: endsAtLevel appears on one ground in src/data/hunt-grounds.js (the Mill Cellar, Level 5). RULED 27-1 (2026-11-20). HYPOTHESIS that the lost hours are small. Read from the journal: hunted hours lost between an outgrown end and the next Start, under Level 16. If it is over an hour a day for new accounts, bring it back.
rows.replaces: None. 27-1 stands. The re-open is refused.
rows.depends: GR-80 (the rest plan and the return card). Chapter 08 section 2.2 drops the "next ground when outgrown" line.

rows.call: Town Works, the Hearthrise event and flame powders become one Great Hearth.
rows.decision: Yes, one landmark and one window with three parts: the Fire (fuel), the Works (gold) and the Colors (powders and named fuels). Fuel only ever moves the Fire and gold never does. The monthly project and its sizing stay exactly as ruled. And one rule for the calendar: weekend 1 IS the Hearthrise. The calendar says when it lights. The server's fire says how big it burns, from +10% Level XP on an empty fire up to +25% on a full one. A full fire is a fixed amount of fuel for each weekly active account.
rows.reason: Three little systems standing around the same fireplace should be one place. And we had two different server XP events, one on a date and one when the fire fills, which could land on top of each other. Making them one thing means feeding the fire all month actually matters for the weekend.
rows.evidence: HYPOTHESIS that one Hearth is more fun than its parts, and that a fire-sized weekend makes people burn fuel. Playtest read: fuel burned in the week before weekend 1 against the week after. The +10% floor is so a quiet server still gets a weekend.
rows.replaces: REVERSAL, small. The 2026-10-25 Hearthrise ruling said the bonus starts when the fire fills. It now lights on the calendar's weekend at the size the fire earned. Fuel only, no gold, and the +25% ceiling stand. 24-10 is NOT reversed: a project a month, sized to the server, with the plaque.
rows.depends: Home decider owns the window and the staged-gift engine (chapter 07 section 2.12). Progression decider: Inner Flame stays a hero skill (GR-61 Kindlings). MM-9 castle rides the same engine. MM-25 timed Level XP cap.

rows.call: No dailies.
rows.decision: Decided at MM-11: no daily quests, no login calendar, no season pass.
rows.reason: Same reason as MM-11. Four heroes turn a daily into four chores.
rows.evidence: See MM-11.

rows.call: The Premium claim needs no press, setups are one idea, and a Week card.
rows.decision: Yes to all three. The Premium daily item lands in Storage on the first visit of the day with no press and the streak never resets. Setups, action sets, presets and the saved kit become one noun, Setup. One Setup for each ground holds the weapon, the worn set, the linings, the bar and the target mode, and it can be copied to another hero or ground (GR-48). A Week card on the first return after the weekly turn compares this week with your last and pays nothing, ever.
rows.reason: A claim button is a press with no decision. Three names for one idea is just confusing. The Week card is a mirror that gives me a reason to look on Monday without turning into a chore.

rows.call: A world boss is one health pool the whole server shares, fought by each account in its own room.

When the window ends the boss leaves whether it fell or not. After each boss the server re-sizes bossPoolPerAccount from what that weekend really earned, aimed at a fall at hour 48, moved at most a quarter each time. The room stays open to the end of the window, so a boss that falls on day one still pays an account whose visits come later (MM-6).

rows.call: Your share of a world boss is counted against your own Level in a room scaled to your party.
rows.decision: Scaled room, yes. But points are not minutes survived. Points = boss bars broken in your room x the tier multiplier from the one tier table. A bar is the scaled boss health for your party Level. When the bar empties it refills and the phases run again (adds at half, enrage at a quarter). A Level 20 four and a Level 300 four earn the same points for the same quality of fight. The room uses the hall formula with the hall number on health only. It does not take the 80 to 90% win target, because its boss never dies. Deaths in the room sit inside the death band of the tier chosen.
rows.reason: If points are just minutes alive then four shield tanks who never swing are the best boss party in the game and my damage means nothing in the one fight the server shares. Counting bars broken makes damage and survival both matter and it lets the boss phases actually play.
rows.evidence: COMPUTED from the formula rule that a mid-geared party breaks a scaled boss in the same time at every Level. HYPOTHESIS until measured. Matrix check: a mid-geared four at Levels 20, 60 and 110 breaks bars an hour within 10% of each other on Normal. If not, the fault is in the boss formula and is fixed there.
rows.depends: GR-27 (the one tier table), GR-30 (boss formula), GR-3 (Deadly sizing). All core and world deciders. Best gear earns about 15% more points, which is the ruled gear size and is intended.

A Level 20 four and a Level 300 four earn the same points for the same quality of fight.

rows.call: A world boss pays a chest by your own points: its own named gear line at your band, its own upgrade material, a 7 day buff, a trophy. No coin.
rows.decision: The chest is by your own points at three marks (about 2, 8 and 20 Normal party-hours). The boss line is four unique pieces, one a style, dropped at the earner's band, on the same budget as the band's best piece with part of it spent on one property. So it is a sidegrade to the band's best, never a tier above it. An account earns at most one line piece a boss weekend. The material trades and feeds only layer pieces (CE-1). Level XP is about a Normal hunt. No coin. The room stays open to the end of the window, and an account's own marks still pay after the boss falls. The fall bonus is paid at the window's end to every account past the first mark, whenever it got there: the 7 day buff (+5% damage dealt) and a re-roll of which line piece the account receives, toward its own heroes' styles. It never adds a second piece.
rows.reason: People want gear and buffs, so that is what it pays. But if my chest and my buff only read my own points then the shared health bar is decoration. Tying the buff and a bonus roll to the fall is what makes me care that other people showed up.

Check E (chest value and XP per stamina hour beside a Normal hunt at Levels 20, 60, 110) and the playtest read "over half of accounts hit the boss on both weekends" overturn them.

rows.call: Collision (c): a death in a world boss room. / A death in the boss room costs the normal death.

Carry on never sends a hero into a boss room. The first send defaults to Normal. Blessings, the ladder and "keep me blessed" apply. The boss card shows the risk reading (deaths per 100 hours for the tier) and what a death would cost this hero before the send. It is one row on the mode table and never a rule for one room. Deaths in the room sit inside the death band of the tier chosen, because the hall number acts on the boss's health and the clock and never on his blows (GR-30). It is built with GR-7 and never before it.

A leader away 14 days passes it on. When the clan finishes its weekly goal every member who gave gets +5% material find (CE-2) for 7 days. A clan never fills a party seat.

rows.call: The castle is one project at a time on the town project engine. Each room carries one standing buff up to the standing caps.
rows.decision: One project at a time on the town project engine, and four rooms of five levels. War room: damage dealt up to +5%. Ward: a Defense rating row sized so a mid-geared four takes up to about 5% less damage an hour (CORE-4). Workshop: town work speed up to +10%. Kitchen: raises the clan's weekly ration cap. A stage can never finish in under a week. castleStagePerMember is sized so a stage takes 1 to 1.3 weeks at the weekly share, which makes twenty stages 20 to 26 weeks. The castle is open at any roster size. No labor, no upkeep, no treasury balance. This changes 31-3 (castle goods keep their built prices) and it is the option Tyler declined on 25-4. A damage buff already makes me level faster, so an XP room is the same thing twice and it is the one room that broke your "clans give no XP" ruling.

But the buff is paid by mark, not by rank. Any clan whose week reaches a set score mark earns a Defense rating buff for the next 7 days, in three steps, sized so a mid-geared four takes up to about 5% less damage an hour (CORE-4). The top three clans get the banner and the plaque on top. Under five clans the board shows a clan against its own last week and the marks still pay.

Playtest read: the share of clans that reach the first mark in week two against week one. If the board is not used by 14 days the board is not built further (chapter 06 section 6).

A fight is about 90 seconds, watched or skipped. The client sends one intent, fight offered opponent 1, 2 or 3, and the server builds both sides and runs it.

Open Arena: heroes as they stand. It reads gear, upgrades, standing buffs and bought boosts under the same caps. It never reads a timed buff that an arena paid. XP and drop buffs do nothing in either.

rows.call: Mixed Levels in one fight follow one visible two thirds line.
rows.decision: Yes. A hero keeps its full share of Level XP if its Level is at least two thirds of the highest Level in the party. Below that it keeps hero Level / (2/3 x top Level). One knob, levelShareLine. The party window says it before the hunt starts. One rule for every party, the boss room included. And the open question from chapter 02: an old ground hunted at your Level takes the LEADER's Level, as ruled, and the party picks its leader.

Survival in those cells is provisional. Check F re-runs the eight carried cells once the engine sends real damage to the back row.

rows.call: Other players on a hunting ground are seen through a presence strip and never fought beside.

One read shows it in three places: the town (heroes at work), a ground's card and hunt view ("3 other parties are hunting here", by leader, clan tag and size), and the world boss page. Each list is short and capped, clan mates and friends first, then nearest Level. Quiet presence leaves you off every list. No shared combat grounds and no 8-person areas.

rows.evidence: COMPUTED estimate about 0.5 database-seconds an account-day or zero if it rides the hunt update (chapter 06). HYPOTHESIS that being seen is enough. Playtest read: four of five players can name something another player did.

rows.call: Every boss, clan, event and arena is open to all. Premium makes timed buffs last a quarter longer and banks arena tickets to 30.

The castle is the long home for it once an account is in a clan. Boss and arena materials bought from other players are a small home. The sizes are the economy decider's.

rows.call: Every buff is a row in one modifier table, and every MMO layer piece sits on the gear curve at the earner's band.
rows.decision: Yes. One table (formula step R20). Rows on one knob sum, then the cap applies. No reward has code of its own. The hero sheet shows one line, for example "Buffs: damage +11% of 15, Level XP +25% of 25". A buff from the same source refreshes and never stacks with itself.
rows.reason: This is the formula-driven game you asked for. If every buff is a row I can read on my sheet, I always know what I have filled and what is left to chase, and nobody has to write special math for a boss or a clan.

rows.call: The buff caps: damage +5% standing and +10% timed, damage taken 5% and 5% less, Level XP +5% and +25%, drop chance +10% timed, town work +10%, no coin buff.
rows.decision: The table with one cut: there is no standing Level XP cap, because no clan room gives XP (MM-9). Damage dealt: +5% standing, +10% timed. Protection: Defense rating rows, sized on the matrix so a mid-geared four takes about 5% less damage an hour standing and about 5% less timed (CORE-4). Level XP: none standing, +25% timed. Material find: none standing, +10% timed, earned only and never sold, with the scope of CE-2. Town work speed: +10% standing. Coin: no buff, ever. Who fills what: the war room, the Ward and the workshop fill the standing caps. Timed damage comes from the boss (+5%) and the Open Arena season (up to +5%). Timed protection comes from the clan board marks. Timed material find comes from the clan weekly goal (+5%) and the Even Arena season (up to +5%). Timed Level XP comes only from the Hearthrise weekend. A ground weekend's featured row (MM-42) is its own event row outside these caps. One check is owed before the protection rows are final: the to-hit formula needs its own floor, so rating rows cannot stack into a second way past the 60% cap.
rows.reason: I want every cap to have a clear way to earn it and no cap that exists for one row. Earned buffs make me kill faster, live longer and find more. Level XP is the weekend for everyone and the thing Crowns buy, which is the engine you described. A coin buff would let money print gold, so never.
rows.evidence: COMPUTED inside the ruled gear sizes (a weapon step is 5% to 8%, best gear about 15%). RULED: +25% event ceiling (27-5), Luck has two feeds only (2026-11-20), so the drop row multiplies after Luck and is never sold. Sizes are TARGET. Check G on the matrix overturns them.
rows.replaces: None. It is what lets 25-2 stand.
rows.depends: Economy decider: MM-29 and MM-30 decide whether a Level XP boost is sold. If it is not, the timed XP cap is full only on the Hearthrise weekend. Core decider: damage taken buffs count inside the 60% mitigation cap. Home decider: the workshop row and the 40% Speed cap.
rows.was: The table as recommended with one cut: there is no standing Level XP cap, because no clan room gives XP (MM-9). Damage dealt: +5% standing, +10% timed. Damage taken: 5% less standing, 5% less timed. Level XP: none standing, +25% timed. Drop chance: none standing, +10% timed and earned only, never sold. Town work speed: +10% standing. Coin: no buff, ever. Who fills what: war room, ward and workshop fill the standing caps. Timed damage comes from the boss (+5%) and the Open Arena season (up to +5%). Timed damage taken comes from the clan board marks. Timed drop chance comes from the clan weekly goal (+5%) and the Even Arena season (up to +5%). Timed Level XP comes only from the Hearthrise weekend and whatever the store sells.

rows.call: The power budget: a fully buffed, boss-geared four gains at most about 32% kill speed and about 72% Level pace over a plain four in mid gear.
rows.decision: One ceiling, written as a reading held by a test and never as a new limit (this keeps ruling 50-11). With every cap full a four reads 1.65 times a plain mid-geared four in Levels an hour and 1.32 in kills an hour. Nobody holds 1.65 outside a Hearthrise weekend, because no Level XP boost is sold. Paying alone, with best gear sooner and a +6% damage boost, reads about 1.22. A player who earns every buff and buys nothing averages about 1.3 times the plain pace over a month. The Level table stays the clock of the plain four and never reads a buff. "Takes 10% less" is read on damage taken an hour.
rows.reason: Buffs have to feel like time gained, so the table is timed on the plain four that everybody has. But the fastest players set when the next region has to be ready, so I want that number honest and as small as it can be while buffs still matter.
rows.evidence: COMPUTED. Ceiling: 1.15 gear x 1.15 damage x 1.25 XP = 1.65. Earned-only average: 1.15 x 1.11 (5% standing, boss 5% for 7 days in 28, arena 5%) x 1.03 (25% for 3 days in 28) = 1.31. Check G overturns it: kill speed 1.25 to 1.40, Level pace 1.5 to 1.7, and no cell where the buffed four holds a tier the plain four cannot enter.
rows.depends: PROGRESSION DECIDER (GR-6): size R1, the region lead, on 1.65 only if the store sells an always-on XP boost, else on about 1.3 to 1.4. ECONOMY DECIDER (MM-31): the paid pace ceiling of 1.60 now sits just under this ceiling and the two should be one number. Art and asset directors for the region schedule.
rows.was: The ceiling is about 32% more kills an hour and about 65% more Levels an hour, not 72%, because the standing XP cap is gone. The Level table stays the clock of the plain four and never reads a buff. And the number chapter 05 asked for: a player who earns every buff and buys nothing averages about 1.3 times the plain pace over a month. Only a player with a bought XP boost running every hour sits at the 1.65 ceiling.
rows.fixNote: The ceiling was written as 1.65 here, 1.58 in MM-31 and 1.60 in the book. MM-31 left out the +5% standing damage row.

rows.call: Boss and arena gear trades like all gear.
rows.decision: Yes. Boss pieces, arena pieces and both materials trade on the market like any gear.
rows.reason: No bound gear is already your rule. Tradeable chase gear is what gives the market something to price and gives people a reason to buy gold with Crowns.

rows.call: The paid advantage
rows.decision: TYLER CONFIRMS. Recommended: paying gives a real edge under a ceiling written in numbers. A payer reaches the ceiling sooner and stays there. A player who does not pay reaches the same ceiling with gold. Nobody passes it.
rows.reason: It is your 2026-11-21 ruling written as a rule. One ceiling for everyone is what keeps the edge real and not broken.
rows.evidence: EVIDENCE: study 49 section 3.1 read ten games with a traded bought currency. Players accept time, membership, capped boosts and looks, and revolt when the store mints power.

rows.call: What the store sells for Crowns
rows.decision: TYLER CONFIRMS. Recommended: Crowns buy Premium, looks and comfort (more market listings). Two timed boosts are sold for gold at the store, in 1 day and 7 day sizes, priced on the wage curve and burned: damage +6%, and a protection boost written on the Defense rating and sized so a mid-geared four takes about 3% less damage an hour. No Level XP boost is sold. Never a drop or material boost, a saved Setup, bag or Storage room, gear, materials, gold, Levels, skill levels, chests, rating, Luck, stamina or any roll. Bound training items join the Crowns store only after the yard fee and to-hit changes are live (ruled 26-10). Sold for gold, the boosts reverse no ruling. If Tyler prefers them sold for Crowns at the same sizes, that reverses the 2026-11-18 line that power is never sold directly for Crowns and it joins the reversal list as row 24.
rows.reason: A traded currency needs something to spend it on every week or its buyers run out, and Premium once a month is not enough. A boost that is also earned in play and sits under the same cap is the mildest direct sale there is. Sizing the bought row under the cap keeps bosses, clans and events worth playing for a payer, because play is the only way to fill the rest.
rows.evidence: COMPUTED: pay alone then reads 1.15 x 1.06 x 1.15, about 40% more Levels an hour over a plain mid-geared four, and 58% with earned buffs on top. HYPOTHESIS that a weekly boost is bought. The alternative is boosts for gold only, which leaves Premium as the one repeating use of a Crown.
rows.replaces: None when the boosts are sold for gold. Sold for Crowns it would reverse the 2026-11-18 line that power is never sold directly for Crowns.
rows.was: TYLER CONFIRMS. Recommended structure: Premium, timed boosts on damage, damage taken and Level XP, comfort (more market listings, more banked arena tickets), looks and bound training items. No drop or material boost (CE-3). No saved setups (GR-56a). No bag or Storage room, which stay gold sinks. Never gear, materials, gold, Levels, skill levels, chests, rating, Luck, stamina or any roll. Boosts come in 1 day and 7 day sizes. One thing needs your explicit yes: a boost sold for Crowns is a direct sale of timed power, which your 11-04 and 11-18 words said would not happen without your word. I recommend yes, with each bought row sized at about 60% of its timed cap (about +15% Level XP, +6% damage, 3% less damage taken).

rows.call: May a bought timed boost fill the Level XP cap? (the 11-04 avoid list against Crowns giving real advantages)

rows.was: TYLER CONFIRMS. Not decided here. My recommendation: no. Bought boosts fill the timed damage cap and nothing on Level XP. The timed Level XP cap of +25% is earned only, from events, world bosses and clans. A payer is then about 27% faster than a plain four through best gear and a damage boost, and anybody who plays the shared world can add the XP on top.

rows.call: Bought boosts and earned buffs
rows.decision: TYLER CONFIRMS. Recommended: they are the same rows in the one modifier table and fill the same timed caps. One bought boost on a knob at a time.
rows.reason: One table and one cap is what makes the ceiling hold without a special rule for money. Earning a buff saves Crowns and buying one never stacks above the cap.
rows.evidence: COMPUTED from MM-24 and MM-25. Read at the settle with a hero's other modifiers, so it adds no server statement (ESTIMATED, study 49).

rows.call: The pace ceiling
rows.decision: TYLER CONFIRMS. Recommended: keep ruling 50-11 (no limit on how much sooner) as it stands and record one reading held by a test, never a new limit. With every cap full a four reads 1.65 times a plain mid-geared four in Levels an hour and 1.32 in kills an hour. Paying alone reads about 1.22. These are the same numbers as MM-26.
rows.reason: You said the limit is on what can be bought, not how fast. The store list and the caps are that limit, and the 58% is just their sum. Writing it as a reading means no ruling of yours is reversed and a test still catches anyone who adds a row that breaks it.
rows.evidence: COMPUTED: 1.15 best gear x 1.10 timed damage x 1.25 timed Level XP = 1.58. On the pace line a band that takes a plain four 10 days takes this four a little over 6.
rows.replaces: None, if taken as a reading. Study 49 wrote it as a re-open of 50-11
depends: GR-6 and MM-26 (whether the Level table is the clock of a plain four, progression decider)
rows.was: TYLER CONFIRMS. Recommended: keep your 2026-11-21 ruling (no limit on how much sooner) as it stands, and record the pace ceiling as a number the caps add up to, held by a test, not as a new limit. A fully boosted, best-geared four gains at most about 58% more Levels an hour than the same four in mid gear with no buffs, and nothing over a non-payer who reached the same caps.
rows.fixNote: The row said 58%. It multiplied 1.15 gear by 1.10 timed damage by 1.25 XP and left out the +5% standing damage of MM-25. With it the product is 1.65.

rows.call: The gear ceiling
rows.decision: TYLER CONFIRMS. Recommended: paying puts a hero 0 bands ahead at any Level, and inside a band at most best gear over mid gear.
rows.reason: Gear is worn by Level only, so gold can buy the best piece of your band and never the next band. That protects the chase.
rows.evidence: COMPUTED from two rulings: gear is worn by Level only, and best gear is about 15% over mid (2026-11-21).

rows.call: The gold ceiling
rows.decision: TYLER CONFIRMS. Recommended: the weekly cap on Crowns an account sells is worth about one account-week of hunting gold at the seller's highest hero Level, so paying at most about doubles a week's gold. The server re-derives the cap in Crowns each week from the 7 day median Crown price.
rows.reason: Every band's sinks cost 1.2 to 1.4 times what the band earns. A payer at double income affords all of them and a free player affords most of them. That is an edge you can feel that buys nothing a free player cannot have. The weekly re-derive keeps "double" true on day 10 and day 600.
rows.evidence: COMPUTED from the sink share target. HYPOTHESIS for the size. It sizes clamp 1 of 24-5, which you already ruled must exist. It is the one true limit on "how much sooner", so it touches 50-11 and is yours.
rows.replaces: None. Sizes a clamp ruled on 2026-11-20

rows.call: The path for players who do not pay
rows.decision: TYLER CONFIRMS. Recommended: everything sold for Crowns can be had with gold through the book. Targets at the book's reference price: Premium for a month is about 3 account-days of gold, and a full week of boosts is about 1.5 account-days. Boost rows scale by the buyer's band so the cost in hours of play holds at every Level.
rows.reason: This is what makes the model fair to a player who never pays, and it is also where a payer's Crowns find their buyers.
rows.evidence: HYPOTHESIS. Players set the real Crown price inside the price band, so each target holds only once the book has run.

rows.call: How Crowns trade
rows.decision: TYLER CONFIRMS. Recommended: a Crown is a number on the account with its own append-only ledger. Crowns are sold for gold on one server-owned book in fixed lots. One trade, then bound. 1% to list and 4% of the gold, both burned. The player-facing name is "Crown Exchange".
rows.reason: One trade then bound means no speculation and no wash loop. The burn makes every Crown sold a gold sink too.
rows.evidence: EVIDENCE: builds 24-5 of 2026-11-20 and the ten-game reading of study 49.

rows.call: The clamps
rows.decision: TYLER CONFIRMS. Recommended: the eight clamps of chapter 04 section 2.8, all inside the Security review before Early Access. One addition: gold paid for Crowns counts against the market's daily spend cap.
rows.reason: A real-money link to gold must not be able to reach another player's economy unchecked.
rows.evidence: EVIDENCE: five clamps are ruled in outline (24-5). Three are added by study 49. The hold days and Steam's wallet rules are open Security questions.

rows.call: Where paying gives no edge
rows.decision: TYLER CONFIRMS. Recommended: no edge in the even arena, in events, or in access to any Level, ground, drop or tier.
rows.reason: It names the places money never reaches, which is what lets a free player trust the rest.
rows.evidence: COMPUTED from the store list (MM-29) and the event rule of CE-8.

rows.call: The open arena matches by gear band, then rating, and thin bands borrow from the next band and from house teams.
rows.decision: Yes. Band first, then rating, three offered. A thin band borrows from the next band up and from that band's house teams.
rows.reason: Gear decides the Open Arena, so I should only meet people in gear like mine. On a small server I would rather fight a house team than wait.
rows.evidence: HYPOTHESIS that it feels fair on a small server. Playtest read: Open Arena fights against real setups over half by week two in the busiest band, and no band where one account wins over 80%.
rows.depends: Items decider (gear bands, GR-4). MM-14.

rows.call: The even arena is one ladder for everyone, with three opponents offered near your rating.
rows.decision: Yes.
rows.reason: Nothing bought or found is read, so one ladder is fair and it is full even at 10 accounts.
rows.evidence: Follows from MM-13.

rows.call: Each arena has its own tickets.
rows.decision: Yes, two pools.
rows.reason: With one pool everyone would spend every ticket in the arena that pays gear and the Even Arena would be empty.
rows.evidence: Design reasoning. HYPOTHESIS. Playtest read: fights in each arena are within a factor of three of each other.

rows.call: Measure once whether the engine can run heroes on both sides of a fight, before either arena is planned.
rows.decision: Yes, and it is the first arena work of any kind. A four against a four on the replay harness: does it run, how long a 90 second fight of eight takes in the edge, and does one style always win. If it fails, both arenas become their own program after the beta and stay hidden.
rows.reason: Both arenas are just a nice idea until we know the engine can put heroes on the enemy side. It is a measurement, so it does not break the no build lanes rule.
rows.evidence: None yet. This row IS the missing evidence (check C).
rows.depends: Systems engineer runs it. MM-12, MM-13, MM-14 wait on it.

rows.call: Events pay buffs and gear: a Level XP weekend, a ground weekend that features its named pieces, boss and arena weekends.
rows.decision: Yes. The between-months ground weekend features that ground's named pieces and does not pay XP. It uses its own event row on that ground's named pieces for that weekend, for everyone hunting that ground. That row is outside the MM-25 caps, is never sold and never stacks with a second event. The rivet allowance is computed without it. The world Level XP weekend stays once in four weekends, as ruled. If the playtest shows a ground weekend does not move people, it goes back to the ruled ground XP weekend.
rows.reason: One XP weekend a month is plenty and a second one just makes everyone level faster than we can build regions. A gear weekend sends the whole server to one ground, so the presence strip is full and new players see veterans there. Named pieces stay worth chasing because they reforge up a band.
rows.evidence: HYPOTHESIS. +10% on a rare is a small pull by itself. The draw is the shared place. Playtest read: hunted hours on the featured ground at least double against the week before. If not, revert to 27-5 as ruled.
rows.replaces: REVERSAL. The second half of 27-5 (2026-11-20, "in between, one party ground gets its own XP weekend"). The first half, the +25% ceiling and "never two at once" all stand.
rows.depends: Items decider: the featured term of the drop formula and which pieces are named (GR-40). GR-9 lets any Level hunt the featured ground. Progression decider: this keeps the timed Level XP cap full only 3 days in 28 for a player who buys nothing.

It fills the timed drop chance cap (+10%) for everyone hunting that ground, on its named pieces only. The world Level XP weekend stays once in four weekends, as ruled. If the playtest shows a ground weekend does not move people, it goes back to the ruled ground XP weekend.

rows.call: For the playtest only, every account gets the same weekly allowance of test Crowns through one server switch.
rows.decision: THIS IS A GRANT. TYLER CONFIRMS. I do not decide it. Recommended: yes, for the wiped Discord playtest only, the same amount for every account, one server switch that is off by default and removed before Early Access, every grant journalled.

rows.call: A standing clan gift (was N6-1).
rows.decision: Yes. A member sets "give my share each Monday" once. The server takes it from the purse each week until it is turned off or the purse cannot pay, and the return card says so.

rows.decision: Yes. One press spends any number of banked tickets with a remembered pick rule, closest rating or highest rating offered. Picking by hand stays.

rows.evidence: The first principle (RULED 2026-10-18).

rows.decision: One system. Capture the flag is a later rule set on the same two arenas, with no death and low XP as you described it on 2026-11-14. Hidden until both sides can be filled.

rows.call: Friends (was N6-4).
rows.decision: A friend is an account, shown by its heroes' names. One request links both accounts and all four heroes on each side see the friend.
rows.reason: Asking four times to add one person is the same decision four times.
rows.evidence: The first principle. RULED 25-7 uses the same per-account shape for clans.
rows.depends: GR-72, MM-20 (friends sort first).

rows.call: The clan's own shared hunt (was N6-5).
rows.decision: When it is built, each party of four fights in its own room and both come off one clan pool, the same form as the world boss. Never eight heroes in one fight. Kept for later and hidden.
rows.reason: One engine runs a party of four. Two rooms on one pool gives a clan its shared hunt without a second engine.
rows.evidence: RULED: one combat engine and one party of four (CLAUDE.md section 6, 25-11).
rows.replaces: REVERSAL, small. The second half of 25-11 ("two parties of four in one hall") becomes two rooms on one clan pool.
rows.depends: MM-2, MM-5.

rows.call: What one Premium gives across four heroes
rows.decision: TYLER CONFIRMS. Recommended contents: the ruled list (12 hour stamina bar on every hero, the full hunt analyzer, Premium looks and one free color change a day, 100 market listings for 14 days), plus one daily 1 hour training item for each hero with the skill pick remembered, the daily claim with no press, and arena tickets banking to 30. Not recommended: "timed buffs last a quarter longer" (MM-21). The risk reading stays free for everyone.
rows.reason: Premium is ruled to never add power, and a buff that lasts longer is more power for the same fight. Everything else on the list is comfort, information or looks, which is what a saver with idle gold will happily buy through the book.
rows.evidence: COMPUTED: the 12 hour bar gives a one-visit player the 12 hunted hours a two-visit player gets free. Four training items a day are about 4% more skill XP a hero under the yard cap of GR-54.
rows.replaces: None. The buff line would break 24-4 of 2026-11-20, which is why it is left out
depends: MM-21 (mmo decider: take the buff line out)
GR-66 and GR-84 (progression and features deciders)

rows.call: The price of Premium and of a Crown
rows.decision: TYLER CONFIRMS. Recommended design: Premium is 30 days, priced in Crowns, at a real-money cost near the genre's monthly membership. A starting number to react to is 8 to 10 dollars a month. Crown lot sizes and the Crown price of each store row are set so that MM-34's targets hold at the book's opening reference price.
rows.reason: Premium does not need to be strong. It needs to be cheap enough in gold that a saver buys it without thinking, because that trade is the one the whole money model rests on.
rows.evidence: HYPOTHESIS. No price has been tested. It is your money call in full.
depends: MM-43 (test Crowns in the playtest are a grant and yours alone)
